card.title: Merciful Lie
card.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The magazine hasn't rejected your poem. They think it deserves its own booklet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They returned it. If even you think it's hopeless, I'll stop writing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's why they returned it. They can't give it enough space.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you write that on the cover? With your name?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Gladly. 'A voice that deserves more space.' Print my name large enough for the editor to see.

mechanism: A protects B's fragile commitment to writing by interpreting returned work as deserving more space and standing behind that claim.
confusable: Unlike denying rejection for convenience, A must show the believed emotional harm and accept growing personal exposure to keep it hidden.
comparison: D15-b lends a signed public endorsement; D15-a takes charge of explaining an invented display-cake concept.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
